outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Welcome back, quiz friends! Grab a pen and keep score. Are you over sixty-five? Then let's check your memory. Fifty questions, from easy to legend. First one: which bird is famous for copying human speech?
lines.a: The parrot! Some African greys learn hundreds of words.

lines.q: What is the capital of Greece?
lines.a: Athens! Named after the goddess Athena.

lines.q: Who wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer?
lines.a: Mark Twain! His real name was Samuel Clemens.

lines.q: Which is the largest continent?
lines.a: Asia! It holds more than half of all the people on Earth.

lines.q: Raisins are dried what?
lines.a: Grapes! Dried plums are prunes. Easy start, right?

lines.q: Which city is home to Big Ben?
lines.a: London! Big Ben is actually the name of the great bell, not the tower.

lines.q: A shuttlecock is used in which sport?
lines.a: Badminton! Real shuttlecocks are made with goose feathers.

lines.q: Which animal is called the ship of the desert?
lines.a: The camel! It can drink over one hundred litres of water in one go.

lines.q: Which country is famous for tulips and windmills?
lines.a: The Netherlands! Funny thing: tulips first came there from Turkey.

lines.q: Mixing blue and yellow paint makes which colour?
lines.a: Green! Ten easy ones done. How many did you get?

lines.q: Now it gets a little harder. What is the longest river in South America?
lines.a: The Amazon! It carries more water than any other river on Earth.

lines.q: Who wrote A Christmas Carol?
lines.a: Charles Dickens! He wrote it in just six weeks.

lines.q: At sea level, water boils at how many degrees Celsius?
lines.a: One hundred! Two hundred and twelve is the Fahrenheit number.

lines.q: Who was the first man to run a mile in under four minutes?
lines.a: Roger Bannister! In nineteen fifty-four, while training to be a doctor.

lines.q: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
lines.a: Tanzania! Many people say Kenya, but it's just over the border.

lines.q: Who played the lead in the nineteen sixty-two film Lawrence of Arabia?
lines.a: Peter O'Toole! It made him a star overnight.

lines.q: What is the currency of Japan?
lines.a: The yen! The won is Korea, the yuan is China.

lines.q: Which scientist gave us the theory of relativity?
lines.a: Albert Einstein! He later turned down the offer to be president of Israel.

lines.q: How many players does a basketball team have on the court?
lines.a: Five! Netball has seven, so that one trips people up.

lines.q: Who sang Rocket Man in nineteen seventy-two?
lines.a: Elton John! Lyrics by his long-time partner Bernie Taupin.

lines.q: Welcome to the hard round! What is the capital of Vietnam?
lines.a: Hanoi! Ho Chi Minh City is bigger, but Hanoi is the capital.

lines.q: Which planet spins tipped over on its side?
lines.a: Uranus! It's tilted almost ninety degrees.

lines.q: Who wrote The Old Man and the Sea?
lines.a: Ernest Hemingway! It helped him win the Nobel Prize.

lines.q: In which year was the Falklands War?
lines.a: Nineteen eighty-two! It lasted about ten weeks.

lines.q: Which country has the most people in Africa?
lines.a: Nigeria! Over two hundred million people. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Who directed Jaws in nineteen seventy-five?
lines.a: Steven Spielberg! He was only twenty-eight.

lines.q: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
lines.a: N A! From the Latin word natrium. Sneaky one, I know.

lines.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of the sea?
lines.a: Neptune! Fitting, because it's a deep blue.

lines.q: The Bermuda Triangle is in which ocean?
lines.a: The Atlantic! Between Florida, Bermuda and Puerto Rico.

lines.q: Which British monarch reigned just before Elizabeth the Second?
lines.a: George the Sixth, her father! Edward the Eighth was before him.

lines.q: Now the very hard round. Who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring?
lines.a: Johannes Vermeer! Painted around sixteen sixty-five in Delft.

lines.q: How many symphonies did Beethoven complete?
lines.a: Nine! He was almost completely deaf when he wrote the ninth.

lines.q: What is the smallest state in the United States?
lines.a: Rhode Island! And it's not even an island.

lines.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
lines.a: About three hundred thousand kilometres per second! Seven times around the Earth in one second.

lines.q: Who was the first US president to resign?
lines.a: Richard Nixon! In nineteen seventy-four, after Watergate.

lines.q: What is the deepest ocean trench on Earth?
lines.a: The Mariana Trench! Mount Everest would fit inside with room to spare.

lines.q: Who wrote Don Quixote?
lines.a: Miguel de Cervantes! Often called the first modern novel.

lines.q: In which year did the Chernobyl disaster happen?
lines.a: Nineteen eighty-six! In Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union.

lines.q: Which scientist wrote the three laws of motion?
lines.a: Isaac Newton! Published in sixteen eighty-seven.

lines.q: What is the largest lake in Africa?
lines.a: Lake Victoria! The Nile flows out of it.

lines.q: Welcome to the legend round! Who composed the waltz The Blue Danube?
lines.a: Johann Strauss the Second! The waltz king of Vienna.

lines.q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
lines.a: Ulaanbaatar! One of the coldest capital cities in the world.

lines.q: Who discovered the electron in eighteen ninety-seven?
lines.a: J J Thomson! He won the Nobel Prize for it.

lines.q: What was the first artificial satellite in space?
lines.a: Sputnik One! Launched by the Soviet Union in nineteen fifty-seven.

lines.q: Which metal has the highest melting point?
lines.a: Tungsten! Over three thousand four hundred degrees Celsius.

lines.q: Who painted the famous melting clocks in The Persistence of Memory?
lines.a: Salvador Dalí! Perfect for a memory quiz, right?

lines.q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings?
lines.a: Ten sixty-six! William the Conqueror won the crown of England.

lines.q: What is the largest moon in our solar system?
lines.a: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter! It's even bigger than the planet Mercury. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude?
lines.a: Gabriel García Márquez! He won the Nobel Prize in nineteen eighty-two.

lines.q: Last one. On which ship did Charles Darwin sail around the world?
lines.a: H M S Beagle! The voyage that led to his theory of evolution.
